findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the finalization ordering/atomicity of the last-pass-ref update relative to lock release (write/advance the authoritative last-pass ref before releasing the lock, or otherwise define the interim state) so a concurrent read-only status/canary snapshot cannot observe a released lock with an un-advanced record and misclassify a just-finished pass.
evidence: Plan: 'writes minimal JSON truth to the Git object named by refs/reconciler/last-pass from a process-level finalization path that runs for both success and process-surviving hard failure'

__main__.py finally (lines 781-788) currently performs release_pass_lock against the latest renewed oid; the plan adds a last-pass-ref write to the same finalization region but does not pin its order relative to release
Status verdict contract distinguishes RUNNING (lock held) from NEVER_RUN (no record and no live lock) — a release-before-record window straddles both
findings.finding: The plan specifies a 'process-level finalization path that runs for both success and process-surviving hard failure' to write the authoritative last-pass ref, but does not specify the ordering/atomicity of that ref update relative to the existing lock-release step that already lives in main()'s finally block. A window in which the lock is released before the last-pass ref advances lets a concurrent read-only status/canary snapshot observe neither a held lock nor an updated record and transiently misclassify (e.g. NEVER_RUN or a spurious STALE) even though the pass just finished.
findings.location: Durable state and writer contract; interacts with __main__.py main() finally block (lines 776-788)
scenarios: A pass finishes; finalization releases the lock, then the last-pass CAS retries/backoff runs; a canary snapshot in that gap sees a free lock and a stale/absent record
Hard-failure finalization writes failure_kind after lock release; a concurrent status read misreads the interim as NEVER_RUN
findings.suggested_fix: State that finalization advances refs/reconciler/last-pass (with its bounded CAS retry) BEFORE releasing refs/reconciler/lock, and define status semantics for the still-possible narrow interim (e.g. a live-lock reading takes precedence, matching the RUNNING contract) so no ordering window yields NEVER_RUN/STALE for a completed pass.

_version.py:138-147 documents the 'reconciler' env_id default as 'the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH shared by the writer (that default) and the reducer's legacy-Jira inference' — so it 'can never drift between the two sides'
findings.finding: The plan's environment-identity premise ('an unset id ... must never default to `reconciler`') does not acknowledge that the codebase already defaults an unset `REBAR_ENV_ID` to the literal `reconciler` in `inbound_translate._event_meta`, sourced from `LEGACY_JIRA_ENV_ID` which `_version.py` documents as the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH the reducer's legacy-Jira channel inference keys on.

A developer pass with unset REBAR_ENV_ID: the plan implies it should become `local:...`, but the existing inbound-event author stamp still writes 'reconciler', creating two conflicting notions of the same identity.

findings.finding: The plan makes 'bridge status' distinguish crashed from running 'via the lock's FENCE (a progress witness observed across one lease)', but the only fence-progress-observation primitive in the codebase (_ref_lock.steal / try_break_if_stale) is a MUTATING CAS that sleeps a full lease; the module deliberately has no read-only expiry helper. A status verb bound by 'reading only DURABLE state' and 'no state mutation' cannot reuse it, and observing fence progress in-band means blocking one lease. The plan does not specify the non-destructive, non-blocking read path status uses to compare the fence across a lease.
findings.location: Design paragraph ('Crashed vs running is answered by refs/reconciler/lock's FENCE ... observed across one lease') and AC 'Crashed is distinguished from running via the lock's fence across one lease'

findings.finding: The AC 'A hard failure is still recorded despite the skipped commit-back step' and 'Crashed is distinguished from running via the fence' rely on TWO different witnesses that the plan does not distinguish. The always-pushed last-pass ref-blob is 'written by the reconciler process itself' — so it captures hard failures the process SURVIVES, but it cannot be written on a SIGKILL/OOM/runner-teardown, which is precisely the crash case the fence must catch. The plan states each mechanism but never ties them: which witness answers which failure class.
findings.location: Design paragraph ('a ref-blob refs/reconciler/last-pass carries the minimal always-pushed truth ... written by the reconciler process itself') and ACs 'A hard failure is still recorded' / 'Crashed is distinguished from running'

findings.finding: The 'canary consumes bridge status' integration depends on the durable ref `refs/reconciler/last-pass` being present in the canary's checkout, but the plan does not state that the canary workflow must fetch `refs/reconciler/*`. The canary workflow currently fetches only the tickets branch; reconcile-bridge.yml, by contrast, explicitly fetches `+refs/reconciler/*:refs/reconciler/*` before reading those refs. Without the same fetch in the canary, `bridge status` reads a locally-absent ref and reports nothing real in CI.
findings.location: Design / AC: 'The canary calls `status` and stops querying the GitHub Actions API for the heartbeat'; reconcile-bridge-canary.yml
findings.suggested_fix: Add a canary-workflow step (mirroring reconcile-bridge.yml:128-136) that runs `git fetch origin '+refs/reconciler/*:refs/reconciler/*' || true` before the `bridge status` invocation, and add an AC asserting the canary reads the reconciler refs it fetched.

findings.finding: The cross-environment safety mechanism keys on REBAR_ENV_ID, but that variable is OPTIONAL and defaults to the shared constant 'reconciler' both in CI (reconcile-bridge.yml:249 `vars.REBAR_ENV_ID || 'reconciler'`) and for a local run with the var unset. A developer running a mutating pass without setting REBAR_ENV_ID writes a durable record stamped 'reconciler' — identical to production — so status treats it as a MATCHING record, not FOREIGN, defeating the acceptance criterion.
findings.location: Plan 'Cross-environment safety' paragraph; AC 'A local run never reports a developer's own pass as production's'
findings.suggested_fix: Have the durable record carry an env stamp that is production-only when it is the CI reconciler (e.g. require the CI workflow to set an explicit non-default REBAR_ENV_ID value, or combine REBAR_ENV_ID with a CI-only marker), and treat an unset/default local stamp as non-matching so status reports it FOREIGN rather than as production.

findings.finding: The Vocabulary-compatibility section asserts 'Current help, workflows, canary code, and docs use rebar bridge status' and frames bridge-status as a 'former spelling' being 'restored' as a delegating alias.
